newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil premiums hold steady in slower volume.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil premiums hold steady in slower volume.

text.p: NWE gas oil premiums were well supported on Wednesday but physical activity maintained this week's more lesiurely tempo, traders said.
Cargo traders attributed the relative lull in activity mainly to slightly easier demand between completion of January programmes and preparation for Feburary business.
Feb IPE gas oil closed 25 cents down at $213.50 a tonne, having recovered from a low of $211.50 triggered by losses on NYMEX crude and products.
German winter grade heating oil was done at Feb IPE +$9 for Jan 20-30 cif NWE, around 50 cents firmer.
French material was around $1 below that level.
A cargo of low sulphur diesel traded unchanged at cif quotes NWE high +$0.25/50 cif Bordeaux. The material was also bid at Feb IPE +$14 into Le Havre, unchanged from late on Tuesday.
Transatlantic arbitrage remains shut but at least four U.S. Gulf cargoes fixed 10 days ago are due in NWE in late January.

Prompt refinery heating oil traded at Feb IPE +$8.50 and +$9 fob Rotterdam, around 50 cents firmer, and Feb IPE +$4.50 for first half February. Some traders see higher numbers at the end of the week on forecasts of colder NWE temperatures.
